tts: In sentences with going to, we do not usually stress to.
We’re going to look after a friend’s daughter.
Are you going to visit someone in hospital?
In negative sentences, we stress not, aren’t and isn’t.
I’m not going to organize an event.

acts.title: Four resolutions, one year later
text: LAST JANUARY they told us their plans. This January we asked what happened.
AIGUL: “I’m going to join a gym.” — She didn’t. “I bought the membership in January and I went four times. This year I’m not going to join anything. I’m going to walk to work instead.”
MARAT: “I’m going to save money.” — He did. “I stopped buying coffee every morning. It sounds small. It was two hundred thousand tenge.”
DANA: “I’m going to take a Spanish course.” — She started in March and stopped in May. “I’m going to try again, but on Saturdays. Tuesday evening was the problem, not Spanish.”
BEKZAT: “I’m not going to make a resolution.” — He kept it perfectly.

write.q: Write your six plans for next year: four things you’re going to do, and two you’re NOT going to do. Give a reason for one of them with because.
write.model: Next year I’m going to take an English course on Saturdays, because Tuesday evening never works for me. I’m going to save money — I’m going to stop buying coffee every morning. I’m going to visit my grandmother more often. I’m going to spend less time on my phone. I’m not going to join a gym; I’m going to walk to work instead. And I’m not going to make any resolutions in December.
